title: Looking for movies with a similar feel to it like "To Catch a Thief"

commenti.body:
Have you seen Charade (1963)? Might not be as similar as you want but in my opinion it is superior. While it wasn’t directed by Hitchcock it is considered the most Hitchcock film he didn’t direct - I’m not sure how accurate it is but it’s a fun caper. 

Cary Grant stars with Audrey Hepburn and they have excellent chemistry.

The setting is Paris not the south of France.
Sounds amazing! We’ll give it a watch for sure! Thanks :)

Charade as already mentioned is very good. The only other Hitchcock that imho has similar vibes it's North by Northwest, although with an American setting. 

Other movies, I'd say How to steal a million (A. Hepburn and Peter O'Toole's caper in Paris), the original Pink Panther (the sequels get more and more slapstick but the first keeps it more balanced), Irma la Douce (similar aesthetic but less crime and more farce), Bell book and candle (not crime, but with fantasy elements), Operazione San Gennaro (Italian caper set in Naples), the original Gambit (caper with Michael Caine and Shirley MacLaine), Topkapi (maybe less romantic, but a great caper with comedy elements). Also The Thin Man and its sequel have that vibe of smooth and romanticism, but in a completely different setting. 

For more recent movies, I'd say A fish called Wanda, Dirty Rotten Scoundrels, Manhattan Murder Mystery, the remake of The Thomas Crown Affair, The man from UNCLE, French Kiss, Entrapment, Ocean's Eleven and its sequels, maybe The Grand Budapest Hotel.

Some good suggestions are already made. Maybe I could add the 2002 Catch Me If You Can to the list. A very enjoyable cat-and-mouse run between a young Leonardo DiCaprio and Tom Hanks, with catchy '60s vibes.

You might also enjoy the 1962 Jules Dassin film *Topkapi,* a light caper movie from which Brian De Palma blatantly lifted the descend-from-the-ceiling heist performed by Tom Cruise in the first *Mission: Impossible* movie.

Use a site like https://tastedive.com/movies/like/To-Catch-A-Thief for similar movies (or books, or other stuff).

The first few rows of recommendations are by Hitchcock, but keep scrolling, and you’ll get to many others.
